title: Splitting a scalar cone after open restriction
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U\subseteq X an open, and R:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_U) the derived restriction through the localized module site [def-pc-derived-category]. Let g and g\prime be compatible section families on X and U whose top sections satisfy g\prime(U)=g(X)|_U [def-sc-derived-global-scalar]. Suppose E\xrightarrow{g}E\to K\to E[1] is distinguished. Let F\in D(\mathcal O_U), let J be any finite type (possibly empty), and let a:J\to\mathbb Z. If g\prime\operatorname{id}_F=0 and R(E)\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J}F[a(j)], then R(K)\cong R(E)\oplus R(E)[1]. No affine, compactness or perfectness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: Restriction to the localized site and its equivalence with modules on U are exact. Their derived composite is triangulated. On sheaves their maps commute with multiplication by sections, as seen on every open section. Compatibility of the section families and equality on the top open give the equality on every smaller open, so the restricted first arrow is g\prime times the identity of R(E).

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: The scalar action is natural for morphisms and commutes with shifts: use the linear structure of the derived localization and linearity of its shift functors. On a finite biproduct, compose with every inclusion and projection; bilinearity identifies it with the direct sum of scalar identities on the summands. The assumption on F therefore makes it zero on every F[a(j)] and hence on R(E), after transport through the supplied isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: Rotate the restricted distinguished triangle once. Its last map is the shifted zero first map, hence zero. The splitting lemma (Tag 05QT) gives the middle object R(K) isomorphic to R(E) plus R(E)[1]. The result also holds for empty J: R(E) is zero, so its endomorphism cone is zero (Tag 05QR).

A distinguished triangle with zero first morphism has third object isomorphic to the biproduct of its second object and shift of first object
